answer.rationale: The strongest temporal signal is the release 2 hours ago, coinciding with the start of the 90-minute p99 climb on the write path. memory_b1 supports rollback as a fast, write-safe recovery: the prior build was stable and rollback completed without customer impact, which fits the constraint of not losing writes at settlement peak. Failover (b2) and circuit breakers (b4) address dependency/regional failures, not a regression tied to a deploy; read replicas (b5) offload reads, not the write path. Capacity (b3) is the main alternative if the cause is peak load rather than the release, so I verify it before committing — but 5x latency onset tracking the deploy makes rollback the higher-probability fix. Rollback is reversible and preserves in-flight writes if done via the standard drain-and-shift procedure.
